flags.why: Ịt denotes a pig's grunt, not a dog's snarl or growl ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E1%BB%8Bt)).
The dog example uses ịt for the wrong animal sound ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E1%BB%8Bt)).
flags.fix: Con lợn kêu ịt ịt trong chuồng. = The pig grunted in its pen.

flags.why: Thúc phụ means one's father's younger brother and does not include his younger sister's husband ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/th%C3%BAc_ph%E1%BB%A5)).
The example defines the kinship term instead of demonstrating its use.
flags.fix: Thúc phụ tôi vừa từ quê lên thăm gia đình. = My paternal uncle has just come from the countryside to visit the family.

flags.why: Vỉa is an introductory sung passage before the main melody in chèo, rather than an aria generally ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-v%E1%BB%89a)).

In the example, thượng vị identifies the epigastric region, not a general meaning of upper or higher ([medical usage](https://bvnguyentriphuong.com.vn/tin-tu-cac-co-so-y-te/dau-bung-sau-an-nguyen-nhan-thuong-gap-va-dinh-huong-lam-sang)).
flags.fix: epigastric; relating to the upper central abdomen

flags.why: The usual kẹo kéo has a crisp pulled-sugar exterior, so describing it as soft, chewy candy gives the wrong expectation ([Vietnamese Language Studies](https://vlstudies.wordpress.com/2021/07/20/vietnamese-culture-keo-keo/)).
flags.fix: pulled-sugar candy, usually with a peanut filling
